headline: Sensex and Nifty recover on value buying; markets log longest weekly losing run since 2020 amid oil concerns

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Value buying in oversold stocks following a sharp market crash on Thursday
Indian crude basket rising above $123 per barrel due to West Asia tensions
Volatility triggered by rising US Treasury yields and domestic bond yields
Concerns over a scheduled three-day bank strike affecting financial services
whatHappening: Sensex closed 315 points higher while Nifty 50 regained the 23,100 level
The Indian Rupee strengthened to 95.80 against the US Dollar
Engineers India was among several stocks that reached new 52-week highs
Despite the daily recovery, Indian shares recorded their longest weekly losing streak since 2020
summary: The Indian stock market bounced back on Friday as the Sensex rose 315 points, supported by value buying in the auto and consumer durables sectors. Despite the daily gain, the market recorded its longest weekly losing run since 2020, pressured by high crude oil prices and rising bond yields. The Rupee also saw a recovery, closing at 95.80 against the U.S. Dollar.
